passages.text: This is the word that the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet concerning Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans: “Announce and declare to the nations; lift up a banner and proclaim it; hold nothing back when you say, ‘Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered, her images are disgraced, her idols are broken in pieces.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke a message about Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans.
The LORD gave this message through Jeremiah the prophet.
Announce this message to the nations.
Declare it openly.
Lift up a banner.
Proclaim the message clearly.
Do not hide anything.
Say these words:
Babylon is captured.
Bel is put to shame.
Marduk is shattered.
Babylon’s images are disgraced.
Babylon’s idols are broken in pieces.
passages.original: הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃ הַגִּ֨ידוּ בַגּוֹיִ֤ם וְהַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ וּֽשְׂאוּ־ נֵ֔ס הַשְׁמִ֖יעוּ אַל־ תְּכַחֵ֑דוּ אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ חַ֣ת מְרֹדָ֔ךְ הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ עֲצַבֶּ֔יהָ חַ֖תּוּ גִּלּוּלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: For a nation from the north will come against her; it will make her land a desolation. No one will live in it; both man and beast will flee.”
passages.sermon:
A nation will come against Babylon.
This nation will come from the north.
This nation will attack Babylon.
This nation will make Babylon’s land empty and ruined.
No one will live in Babylon.
No person will remain there.
No animal will remain there.
All people will leave Babylon.
All animals will leave Babylon.
passages.original: כִּ֣י עָלָה֩ עָלֶ֨יהָ גּ֜וֹי מִצָּפ֗וֹן הֽוּא־ יָשִׁ֤ית אֶת־ אַרְצָהּ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּ֑הּ מֵאָדָ֥ם וְעַד־ בְּהֵמָ֖ה נָ֥דוּ הָלָֽכוּ׃

passages.text: “In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the children of Israel and the children of Judah will come together, weeping as they come, and will seek the LORD their God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
He makes a promise about the future.
He says, “In those days and at that time, this will happen.
The children of Israel will come.
The children of Judah will come too.
They will come together.
They will walk together.
They will weep as they come.
They will seek the LORD their God.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֨ים הָהֵ֜מָּה וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה יָבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הֵ֥מָּה וּבְנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו הָל֤וֹךְ וּבָכוֹ֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will come and join themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel and Judah will seek the way to Zion.
They will ask for directions to Zion.
They will turn their faces toward Zion.
They will come to Zion.
They will join themselves to the LORD.
They will make an everlasting covenant with the LORD.
This covenant will never be forgotten.
passages.original: צִיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֔לוּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הֵ֣נָּה פְנֵיהֶ֑ם בֹּ֚אוּ וְנִלְו֣וּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃ס

passages.text: My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray, causing them to roam the mountains. They have wandered from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel and Judah.
God calls His people lost sheep.
Their leaders are their shepherds.
Their shepherds led them astray.
The people wandered on the mountains.
They went from one mountain to another hill.
They forgot where they should rest.
passages.original: צֹ֤אן אֹֽבְדוֹת֙ הָיָה עַמִּ֔י רֹעֵיהֶ֣ם הִתְע֔וּם הָרִ֖ים שׁוֹבֵבִים מֵהַ֤ר אֶל־ גִּבְעָה֙ הָלָ֔כוּ שָׁכְח֖וּ רִבְצָֽם׃

passages.text: All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said, ‘We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.’
passages.sermon:
God’s people are like lost sheep.
Their enemies found them.
Their enemies devoured them.
Their enemies said, “We are not guilty.”
They said this because God’s people sinned against the LORD.
The LORD is their true pasture.
The LORD is the hope of their fathers.
passages.original: כָּל־ מוֹצְאֵיהֶ֣ם אֲכָל֔וּם וְצָרֵיהֶ֥ם אָמְר֖וּ לֹ֣א נֶאְשָׁ֑ם תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטְא֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ נְוֵה־ צֶ֔דֶק וּמִקְוֵ֥ה אֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Flee from the midst of Babylon; depart from the land of the Chaldeans; be like the he-goats that lead the flock.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God’s people live in Babylon.
God commands His people to flee from Babylon.
God tells them to leave the land of the Chaldeans.
God wants them to go out quickly.
God tells them to lead others.
God says, “Be like the he-goats that go before the flock.”
He-goats lead the sheep.
God’s people must lead others out.
passages.original: נֻ֚דוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים יָצְאוּ וִהְי֕וּ כְּעַתּוּדִ֖ים לִפְנֵי־ צֹֽאן׃

passages.text: For behold, I stir up and bring against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will line up against her; from the north she will be captured. Their arrows will be like skilled warriors who do not return empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God says, “I will act against Babylon.
I will gather many nations.
These nations will come from the land of the north.
I will bring these nations together as one group.
They will prepare for battle against Babylon.
They will attack Babylon from the north.
Babylon will be captured by them.
Their arrows will strike like skilled warriors.
These warriors will not miss their target.
They will not return without success.
They will not come back empty-handed.
passages.original: כִּ֣י הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֡י מֵעִיר֩ וּמַעֲלֶ֨ה עַל־ בָּבֶ֜ל קְהַל־ גּוֹיִ֤ם גְּדֹלִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְעָ֣רְכוּ לָ֔הּ מִשָּׁ֖ם תִּלָּכֵ֑ד חִצָּיו֙ כְּגִבּ֣וֹר מַשְׁכִּ֔יל לֹ֥א יָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃

passages.text: Chaldea will be plundered; all who plunder her will have their fill,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD declares this message.
Chaldea is a nation.
Enemies will plunder Chaldea.
Those who plunder Chaldea will take much.
They will be satisfied with what they take.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָ֥ה כַשְׂדִּ֖ים לְשָׁלָ֑ל כָּל־ שֹׁלְלֶ֥יהָ יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Because you rejoice, because you sing in triumph— you who plunder My inheritance— because you frolic like a heifer treading grain and neigh like stallions, your mother will be greatly ashamed; she who bore you will be disgraced. Behold, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a nation that plunders God's inheritance.
Babylon rejoices and sings in triumph.
Babylon acts like a young heifer that frolics while treading grain.
Babylon neighs loudly like strong stallions.
Babylon's mother will feel great shame.
The one who gave birth to Babylon will be disgraced.
Babylon will become the least of all nations.
Babylon will become a wilderness.
Babylon will become a dry land.
Babylon will become a desert.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תִשְׂמְחִי כִּ֣י תַעֲלְזִי שֹׁסֵ֖י נַחֲלָתִ֑י כִּ֤י תָפוּשִׁי כְּעֶגְלָ֣ה דָשָׁ֔ה וְתִצְהֲלִי כָּאֲבִּרִֽים׃ בּ֤וֹשָׁה אִמְּכֶם֙ מְאֹ֔ד חָפְרָ֖ה יֽוֹלַדְתְּכֶ֑ם הִנֵּה֙ אַחֲרִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם מִדְבָּ֖ר צִיָּ֥ה וַעֲרָבָֽה׃

passages.text: Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited; she will become completely desolate. All who pass through Babylon will be horrified and will hiss at all her wounds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is angry.
Because of the LORD’s wrath, Babylon will not have people living in it.
Babylon will become empty and ruined.
No one will live there.
Anyone who passes through Babylon will be shocked.
They will see Babylon’s wounds.
They will hiss at all her injuries.
passages.original: מִקֶּ֤צֶף יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א תֵשֵׁ֔ב וְהָיְתָ֥ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה כֻּלָּ֑הּ כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עַל־ בָּבֶ֔ל יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־ כָּל־ מַכּוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Line up in formation around Babylon, all you who draw the bow! Shoot at her! Spare no arrows! For she has sinned against the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a great city.
Babylon has sinned against the LORD.
All archers must gather around Babylon.
All who draw the bow must take their place.
Aim your arrows at Babylon.
Do not hold back any arrows.
Shoot at Babylon without mercy.
passages.original: עִרְכ֨וּ עַל־ בָּבֶ֤ל׀ סָבִיב֙ כָּל־ דֹּ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת יְד֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ אַֽל־ תַּחְמְל֖וּ אֶל־ חֵ֑ץ כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָֽאָה׃

passages.text: Raise a war cry against her on every side! She has thrown up her hands in surrender; her towers have fallen; her walls are torn down. Since this is the vengeance of the LORD, take out your vengeance upon her; as she has done, do the same to her.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is bringing vengeance against Babylon.
Babylon is surrounded by enemies.
Raise a war cry against Babylon from every side.
Babylon has surrendered.
She has lifted her hands in defeat.
Her towers have fallen down.
Her walls are destroyed.
This is the LORD’s vengeance.
Take vengeance on Babylon.
Do to her as she has done to others.
passages.original: הָרִ֨יעוּ עָלֶ֤יהָ סָבִיב֙ נָתְנָ֣ה יָדָ֔הּ נָֽפְלוּ֙ אַשְׁוִיֹּתֶיהָ נֶהֶרְס֖וּ חֽוֹמוֹתֶ֑יהָ כִּי֩ נִקְמַ֨ת יְהוָ֥ה הִיא֙ הִנָּ֣קְמוּ בָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. In the face of the oppressor’s sword, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is the subject.
Babylon has people who sow seed.
Babylon has people who harvest with a sickle.
Remove the sower from Babylon.
Remove the harvester from Babylon at harvest time.
An oppressor brings a sword against Babylon.
Because of the oppressor’s sword, each person will turn to his own people.
Each person will flee to his own land.
passages.original: כִּרְת֤וּ זוֹרֵ֙עַ֙ מִבָּבֶ֔ל וְתֹפֵ֥שׂ מַגָּ֖ל בְּעֵ֣ת קָצִ֑יר מִפְּנֵי֙ חֶ֣רֶב הַיּוֹנָ֔ה אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־ עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֻֽסוּ׃ס

passages.text: Israel is a scattered flock, chased away by lions. The first to devour him was the king of Assyria; the last to crush his bones was Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.”
passages.sermon:
Israel is like a flock of sheep.
This flock is scattered.
Lions have chased Israel away.
The king of Assyria was the first lion.
The king of Assyria devoured Israel.
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar was the last lion.
Nebuchadnezzar crushed Israel’s bones.
passages.original: שֶׂ֧ה פְזוּרָ֛ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲרָי֣וֹת הִדִּ֑יחוּ הָרִאשׁ֤וֹן אֲכָלוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְזֶ֤ה הָאַחֲרוֹן֙ עִצְּמ֔וֹ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “I will punish the king of Babylon.
I will punish the land of Babylon.
I punished the king of Assyria before.
I will punish the king of Babylon in the same way.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֥י פֹקֵ֛ד אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאֶל־ אַרְצ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקַ֖דְתִּי אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: I will return Israel to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God promises to bring Israel back to his own land.
Israel will return to his pasture.
Israel will eat and be safe on Mount Carmel.
Israel will eat and be safe in Bashan.
Israel will find satisfaction on the hills of Ephraim.
Israel will find satisfaction on the hills of Gilead.
passages.original: וְשֹׁבַבְתִּ֤י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ נָוֵ֔הוּ וְרָעָ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַבָּשָׁ֑ן וּבְהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֛יִם וְהַגִּלְעָ֖ד תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, a search will be made for Israel’s guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah’s sins, but they will not be found; for I will forgive the remnant I preserve.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He says, “In those days and at that time, I will act.”
People will search for Israel’s guilt.
They will not find any guilt in Israel.
People will look for Judah’s sins.
They will not find any sins in Judah.
I will forgive the people I have kept alive.
I will show mercy to the remnant I preserve.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֩ וּבָעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֗ה יְבֻקַּ֞שׁ אֶת־ עֲוֺ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־ חַטֹּ֥את יְהוּדָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִמָּצֶ֑אינָה כִּ֥י אֶסְלַ֖ח לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אַשְׁאִֽיר׃

passages.text: Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the residents of Pekod. Kill them and devote them to destruction. Do all that I have commanded you,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD commands action.
Go up against the land of Merathaim.
Attack the people who live in Pekod.
Kill them.
Devote them to destruction.
Do everything I have commanded you.
This is the declaration of the LORD.
passages.original: עַל־ הָאָ֤רֶץ מְרָתַ֙יִם֙ עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֶל־ יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּק֑וֹד חֲרֹ֨ב וְהַחֲרֵ֤ם אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲשֵׂ֕ה כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: “The noise of battle is in the land— the noise of great destruction.
passages.sermon:
There is a sound in the land.
This sound is the noise of battle.
There is also the sound of great destruction.
The land is filled with these sounds.
passages.original: ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְשֶׁ֖בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: How the hammer of the whole earth lies broken and shattered! What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!
passages.sermon:
Babylon was powerful.
Babylon was like a hammer to the whole earth.
Now Babylon is broken.
Now Babylon is shattered.
Babylon has become a horror.
Babylon is a horror among the nations.
passages.original: אֵ֤יךְ נִגְדַּע֙ וַיִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר פַּטִּ֖ישׁ כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: I laid a snare for you, O Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and captured because you challenged the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a powerful nation.
Babylon challenged the LORD.
The LORD laid a trap for Babylon.
Babylon did not know about the trap.
Babylon was caught in the trap.
The LORD found Babylon.
The LORD captured Babylon.
Babylon was captured because it challenged the LORD.
passages.original: יָקֹ֨שְׁתִּי לָ֤ךְ וְגַם־ נִלְכַּדְתְּ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאַ֖תְּ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עַתְּ נִמְצֵאת֙ וְגַם־ נִתְפַּ֔שְׂתְּ כִּ֥י בַֽיהוָ֖ה הִתְגָּרִֽית׃

passages.text: The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath, for this is the work of the Lord GOD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD has an armory.
The LORD opened His armory.
The LORD brought out His weapons of wrath.
The LORD is acting in the land of the Chaldeans.
This is the LORD’s work.
The LORD is doing this in the land of the Chaldeans.
passages.original: פָּתַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ א֣וֹצָר֔וֹ וַיּוֹצֵ֖א אֶת־ כְּלֵ֣י זַעְמ֑וֹ כִּי־ מְלָאכָ֣ה הִ֗יא לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

passages.text: Come against her from the farthest border. Break open her granaries; pile her up like mounds of grain. Devote her to destruction; leave her no survivors.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a powerful nation.
God commands her enemies to attack her.
Come against Babylon from the farthest border.
Break open her granaries.
Pile her up like mounds of grain.
Devote Babylon to destruction.
Leave her no survivors.
passages.original: בֹּֽאוּ־ לָ֤הּ מִקֵּץ֙ פִּתְח֣וּ מַאֲבֻסֶ֔יהָ סָלּ֥וּהָ כְמוֹ־ עֲרֵמִ֖ים וְהַחֲרִימ֑וּהָ אַל־ תְּהִי־ לָ֖הּ שְׁאֵרִֽית׃

passages.text: Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come— the time of their punishment.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Babylon.
Babylon has young bulls.
Kill all her young bulls.
Let them go down to the slaughter.
Woe comes upon them.
Their day has arrived.
This is the time of their punishment.
passages.original: חִרְבוּ֙ כָּל־ פָּרֶ֔יהָ יֵרְד֖וּ לַטָּ֑בַח ה֣וֹי עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ בָ֥א יוֹמָ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Listen to the fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon, declaring in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for His temple.
passages.sermon:
Fugitives and refugees come from the land of Babylon.
They speak in Zion.
They declare the vengeance of the LORD.
The LORD is our God.
He brings vengeance for His temple.
passages.original: ק֥וֹל נָסִ֛ים וּפְלֵטִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ בָּבֶ֑ל לְהַגִּ֣יד בְּצִיּ֗וֹן אֶת־ נִקְמַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Summon the archers against Babylon, all who string the bow. Encamp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a powerful and arrogant nation.
God commands people to gather many archers against Babylon.
All who can use a bow must come.
They must surround Babylon on every side.
No one must escape from Babylon.
God commands them to repay Babylon for her actions.
They must do to Babylon what she has done to others.
Babylon has acted proudly against the LORD.
Babylon has defied the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ אֶל־ בָּבֶ֣ל׀ רַ֠בִּים כָּל־ דֹּ֨רְכֵי קֶ֜שֶׁת חֲנ֧וּ עָלֶ֣יהָ סָבִ֗יב אַל־ יְהִיָ֙־ פְּלֵטָ֔ה שַׁלְּמוּ־ לָ֣הּ כְּפָעֳלָ֔הּ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־ לָ֑הּ כִּ֧י אֶל־ יְהוָ֛ה זָ֖דָה אֶל־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Therefore, her young men will fall in the streets, and all her warriors will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD declares this message.
Babylon is the subject.
Babylon’s young men will fall in the streets.
All Babylon’s warriors will be silenced on that day.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתָּ֥הּ יִדַּ֛מּוּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Behold, I am against you, O arrogant one,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, “for your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “I am against you, arrogant one.
Your day has come.
This is the time I will punish you.”
passages.original: הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ זָד֔וֹן נְאֻם־ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֛י בָּ֥א יוֹמְךָ֖ עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The arrogant one will stumble and fall with no one to pick him up. And I will kindle a fire in his cities to consume all those around him.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord of Hosts speaks against the arrogant one.
The arrogant one will stumble.
The arrogant one will fall.
No one will help him rise.
I, the Lord, will start a fire in his cities.
The fire will destroy everything around him.
passages.original: וְכָשַׁ֤ל זָדוֹן֙ וְנָפַ֔ל וְאֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ מֵקִ֑ים וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֖ה כָּל־ סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah as well. All their captors hold them fast, refusing to release them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He is the God who commands armies.
The sons of Israel are oppressed.
The sons of Judah are also oppressed.
Their captors hold them tightly.
Their captors refuse to let them go.
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עֲשׁוּקִ֛ים בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל וּבְנֵי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו וְכָל־ שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ בָ֔ם מֵאֲנ֖וּ שַׁלְּחָֽם׃

passages.text: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name. He will fervently plead their case so that He may bring rest to the earth, but turmoil to those who live in Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The Redeemer of Israel and Judah is strong.
His name is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts will fight for Israel and Judah.
He will plead their case with great power.
He will bring rest to the earth.
He will bring trouble to the people who live in Babylon.
passages.original: גֹּאֲלָ֣ם׀ חָזָ֗ק יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שְׁמ֔וֹ רִ֥יב יָרִ֖יב אֶת־ רִיבָ֑ם לְמַ֙עַן֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעַ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִרְגִּ֖יז לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: A sword is against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD, against those who live in Babylon, and against her officials and wise men.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He is strong and powerful.
He declares judgment.
A sword is against the Chaldeans.
A sword is against the people who live in Babylon.
A sword is against Babylon’s officials.
A sword is against Babylon’s wise men.
passages.original: חֶ֥רֶב עַל־ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־ שָׂרֶ֖יהָ וְאֶל־ חֲכָמֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: A sword is against her false prophets, and they will become fools. A sword is against her warriors, and they will be filled with terror.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God is strong.
God brings judgment against Babylon.
God sends a sword against Babylon’s false prophets.
The false prophets will become fools.
God sends a sword against Babylon’s warriors.
The warriors will be filled with terror.
passages.original: חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־ הַבַּדִּ֖ים וְנֹאָ֑לוּ חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־ גִּבּוֹרֶ֖יהָ וָחָֽתּוּ׃

passages.text: A sword is against her horses and chariots and against all the foreigners in her midst, and they will become like women. A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered.
passages.sermon:
God speaks against Babylon.
God sends a sword against Babylon’s horses.
God sends a sword against Babylon’s chariots.
God sends a sword against all the foreigners living inside Babylon.
These foreigners will become weak and fearful like women.
God sends a sword against Babylon’s treasuries.
Enemies will plunder Babylon’s treasures.
passages.original: חֶ֜רֶב אֶל־ סוּסָ֣יו וְאֶל־ רִכְבּ֗וֹ וְאֶל־ כָּל־ הָעֶ֛רֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖הּ וְהָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־ אוֹצְרֹתֶ֖יהָ וּבֻזָּֽזוּ׃

passages.text: A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up. For it is a land of graven images, and the people go mad over idols.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a land filled with idols.
A drought will strike Babylon’s waters.
Her waters will dry up.
The people in Babylon worship idols.
The people act foolishly because of their idols.
passages.original: חֹ֥רֶב אֶל־ מֵימֶ֖יהָ וְיָבֵ֑שׁוּ כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ פְּסִלִים֙ הִ֔יא וּבָאֵימִ֖ים יִתְהֹלָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: So the desert creatures and hyenas will live there and ostriches will dwell there. It will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.
passages.sermon:
Desert creatures will live there.
Hyenas will also live there.
Ostriches will dwell there.
No people will ever live there again.
No one will settle there for all generations.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן יֵשְׁב֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־ אִיִּ֔ים וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֖הּ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ תֵשֵׁ֥ב עוֹד֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכּ֖וֹן עַד־ דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃

passages.text: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors,” declares the LORD, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.
passages.sermon:
God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
God also destroyed their neighboring cities.
The LORD declares this.
No person will live there.
No human will stay there.
passages.original: כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־ סְדֹ֧ם וְאֶת־ עֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאֶת־ שְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־ יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־ אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, an army is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
A powerful army is coming.
This army comes from the north.
A great nation leads them.
Many kings join them.
These kings come from distant parts of the earth.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מִצָּפ֑וֹן וְג֤וֹי גָּדוֹל֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים יֵעֹ֖רוּ מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against you, O Daughter of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The army comes against Babylon.
The soldiers hold bows.
They also hold spears.
These soldiers are cruel.
They do not show mercy.
Their voices roar like the sea.
They ride on horses.
They stand in formation for battle.
They come against you, Daughter of Babylon.
passages.original: קֶ֣שֶׁת וְכִידֹ֞ן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הֵ֙מָּה֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָם֙ כַּיָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְעַל־ סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת־ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: The king of Babylon has heard the report, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon hears the news.
His hands become weak and powerless.
Anguish takes hold of him.
He feels pain like a woman giving birth.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֧ע מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־ שִׁמְעָ֖ם וְרָפ֣וּ יָדָ֑יו צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Babylon from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks these words.
The LORD is powerful and unmatched.
A destroyer will come up like a lion.
The lion rises from the thickets of the Jordan.
The lion comes to a rich, safe pasture.
The LORD will quickly drive Babylon from her land.
The LORD will appoint a chosen one for this task.
No one is like the LORD.
No one can challenge the LORD.
No shepherd can stand before the LORD.
passages.original: הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־ נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־ אַרְגִּ֤עָה אֲרוּצֵם מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֙וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יוֹעִדֶ֔נִּי וּמִֽי־ זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃

passages.text: Therefore hear the plans that the LORD has drawn up against Babylon and the strategies He has devised against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has made plans against Babylon.
The LORD has devised strategies against the land of the Chaldeans.
Listen to these plans.
The LORD will act.
The young ones of the flock will be dragged away.
Their pasture will become desolate because of them.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־ בָּבֶ֔ל וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים אִם־ לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־ לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נָוֶֽה׃

passages.text: At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake; a cry will be heard among the nations.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a powerful city.
God will judge Babylon.
People will capture Babylon.
The sound of Babylon’s fall will be loud.
The earth will shake when Babylon is captured.
People in many nations will hear a cry.
This cry will spread among all the nations.
passages.original: מִקּוֹל֙ נִתְפְּשָׂ֣ה בָבֶ֔ל נִרְעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וּזְעָקָ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִ֥ם נִשְׁמָֽע׃ס
